title: Reducedness after tensoring with an algebraic closure is independent of the chosen closure
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and let $\bar k/k$ be any algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Then $A\otimes_k\bar k$ is reduced if and only if $A\otimes_k\operatorname{AlgebraicClosure}(k)$ is reduced, where $\operatorname{AlgebraicClosure}(k)$ is Mathlib’s canonical algebraic closure.

source.place: Tag 09GV (algebraic closures are isomorphic over the base field), with tensor-product transport of reducedness

proof.text: By the algebraic-closure uniqueness statement [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique] (Stacks Tag 09GV), the given algebraic closure $\bar k$ and Mathlib's canonical algebraic closure $\operatorname{AlgebraicClosure}(k)$ are isomorphic as field extensions of $k$. Thus choose a $k$-algebra equivalence $e:\bar k\simeq_k\operatorname{AlgebraicClosure}(k)$; its commutation with the structure maps is exactly the over-$k$ condition.

Apply [lem-trf-reducedness-tensor-alg-equiv] to the $k$-algebra equivalence $e$ and the identity equivalence of $A$. Its stated conclusion is exactly that $A\otimes_k\bar k$ is reduced if and only if $A\otimes_k\operatorname{AlgebraicClosure}(k)$ is reduced. The underlying transport is the ring equivalence induced by `Algebra.TensorProduct.congr`; the equivalence and its inverse are injective, so `isReduced_of_injective` gives the two implications. Therefore the required equivalence holds.
